content: Very cool! The paper states that this is stronger than lean's inductive types, which seems worth emphasizing.

The paper presents a class of inductive types which is arguably stronger than Lean's yes, although this library does not make any attempt at said extending class (this would require touching the kernel), and instead simply takes inspiration of the way they construct their recursors to build them in Lean for better use of the induction tactic.
An ignorant question: what do you mean here by "a class that is stronger (than another)"?

I am not talking about logical strength here but rather expressivity, The aforementioned paper (as well as Rocq, where the work has been done) accepts more nested inductive types than Lean. In particular, lean refuses any nested type in which a free variable appears in one of it's nested occurrences, so types like these are rejected by Lean but accepted in the paper's presentation/Rocq:

inductive DepthTree : Nat → Type
  | foo : List (DepthTree n) → DepthTree (n+1)
